storyboard.claim: A bomb could neutralize Ophus' mind control and save thousands of lives.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon: one figure controlling others, the control the bomb must stop.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the flame root bomb Arrow reported to Luther.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the bomb itself is not drawn; the icon shows only the control it targets.
storyboard.staging: Luther thinks it over, worried, as the control icon appears.

explainedBy: The test requires cutting Luther's own hand, so Luther is the one being asked to take the cut.

storyboard.claim: The test is a tiny cut on Luther's hand.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther, worried, thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the bomb's purpose.
storyboard.addedInformation: The test is aimed at Luther himself.

storyboard.claim: Luther flatly refuses the test and snaps at her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther angrily points away, rejecting the proposal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Luther's reaction to the cut test.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the refusal as anger, not as calm reasoning.
storyboard.staging: Luther, angry, points off-screen and refuses.

callout.text: Refuses to risk even a paper cut

storyboard.claim: Luther protects his magic from even a tiny, brief loss.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon: protection, the magic he guards.
storyboard.onScreenText: Refuses to risk even a paper cut
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why Luther refused the test.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the protective motive visible through the shield.
storyboard.staging: Luther, angry, guards the magic the shield stands for.

explainedBy: Luther's risk-aversion is set against Diem's need for him after her escape, a relation between two people with the heart icon as devotion.

storyboard.claim: Luther's fear of being incapacitated is reckless when Diem needs him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther and Diem in a two-shot with a heart icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the reason for the refusal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Diem is the reason for the risk-aversion.

storyboard.claim: Luther puts protecting one woman above a weapon that could save the continent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heart icon: the bond to one woman, set against the wider stakes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the reckless choice from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the trade-off visible: love is the thing put first.
storyboard.staging: Luther, worried, points at the heart icon as the priority.

storyboard.claim: The romance may weaken the political and military stakes of the book.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heart icon: the romance the narrator questions.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the example into a question about the whole book.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames romance as the question, not as a verdict.
storyboard.staging: Luther, neutral, pondering beside the romance icon.

explainedBy: Love (the bond) is set against the realm the generals should defend, shown by a city icon as the realm.

storyboard.claim: The generals put love over the realm they should serve.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A city icon with Luther.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the question as a critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: The city stands for the realm.

explainedBy: The fair critique judges the generals as flawed, staged as a sad figure accepting the flaw.

storyboard.claim: The generals are flawed and unpredictable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther sad, slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Accepts the critique from beat 247.
storyboard.addedInformation: The flaw is named as a fair judgement.

storyboard.claim: The author's writing lifts the whole genre.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host-only beat with no figure: the callout carries the claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the critique to the writing's achievement.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no picture of the writing itself; the callout is the content.
storyboard.staging: No character on screen; the callout speaks.

explainedBy: The shared flaw of Diem and Luther is the cause that breaks the violent cycle, shown as a two-person pairing.

storyboard.claim: The same flaw lets them break the cycle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Diem and Luther in a two-shot.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the critique into a reframing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The flaw is the cause of the cycle's end.

explainedBy: The reframing is an insight, shown by a lightbulb as the realization that the flaw is the cure.

storyboard.claim: The reframing is the crucial insight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lightbulb icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Announces the reframing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The insight is that flaws enable change.

storyboard.claim: The original Kindred destroyed the world through their own control.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host-only beat with no figure: a destroyed world cannot be drawn intact, so the callout carries it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the Kindred comparison with a question.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the destruction is only spoken.
storyboard.staging: No character on screen; the callout speaks.

storyboard.claim: The Kindred systematically controlled their grief and their bonds.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon: one force controlling others, set on the temple stage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the Kindred destroyed the world.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the control literal: the Kindred act on their bonds.
storyboard.staging: The puppeteer icon stands on the temple stage.

storyboard.claim: Trying to control the bond ended in endless war and oppression.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from controlling the bond to endless war.
storyboard.onScreenText: CONTROLLING THE BOND ENDS IN WAR
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the Kindred's method and its result.
storyboard.addedInformation: The flow shows cause and effect in one picture.
storyboard.staging: Diagram only: the cause leads to the effect.

storyboard.claim: Diem and Luther do not manage or hide from their bond; they face it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heart icon: the bond they face, with Luther neutral beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts with the Kindred's control.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the rejected approach; the heart shows what they face instead.
storyboard.staging: Luther, neutral, beside the heart icon; the struck callout is the method they reject.

storyboard.claim: Through their bond, they burn the corrupt system to the ground.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fire icon: the bond burning the old system down.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows from facing the bond.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fire is the rebellion the bond ignites.
storyboard.staging: Luther, angry, points at the fire that brings the system down.

storyboard.claim: For this Crown, the bond is the war itself, not a distraction from it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon with Luther neutral beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the distraction question.
storyboard.addedInformation: The war icon makes the bond the war's subject.
storyboard.staging: Luther, neutral, stands beside the war icon.

storyboard.claim: The old god at the Everflame states the cosmic law.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Everflame icon, the sacred flame where the law is spoken.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the question the hosts were leading to.
storyboard.addedInformation: The own icon shows the Everflame where the law was stated.
storyboard.staging: The Everflame stands on the temple stage.

storyboard.claim: The magic demands a life in exchange for a life to balance the spell.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance icon: two sides weighed, an exchange of lives.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the law stated in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The balance shows the exchange as an even trade.
storyboard.staging: The balance icon stands on the temple stage.

explainedBy: Diem walking away from heaven toward the mortal realm is the choice the narration describes.

storyboard.claim: Diem may turn her back on heaven for Luther.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Diem walking, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the law to Diem.
storyboard.addedInformation: The choice is leaving heaven.

explainedBy: Diem, afraid and thinking, faces the question of who bears the cost of her choice.

storyboard.claim: Someone must pay the terrible price for her choice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Diem afraid, thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the question of cost.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cost is unknown.

callout.text: Long after the embers burn out

storyboard.claim: The question stays with the viewer long after the video ends.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fire icon: the embers of the closing image.
storyboard.onScreenText: Long after the embers burn out
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the chapter on the question.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fire recalls the Everflame and its unresolved cost.
storyboard.staging: The fire icon fades on an abstract set.
